title: Classes in Header Files and Nested Types
summary: Put the **class definition** in `Name.h` and the **member function bodies** in `Name.cpp`, written as `ClassName::function`. Small functions can stay in the header. Types can be nested inside a class, as in `Player::State`.
ideas:
1. Split a `BankAccount` class into a header and a source file.
2. Give a `TrafficLight` class a nested `enum class Color` and a nested `struct Timing`.
3. Create two classes that refer to each other by pointer, using forward declarations.

cards.q: How do you define a member function outside the class?
cards.a:
`ReturnType ClassName::function(parameters) const { ... }`

The `ClassName::` prefix says which class the function belongs to. Without it you define an unrelated free function.

cards.q: Why must templates be defined entirely in headers?
cards.a:
Every file that uses a template needs its full definition

Each file that uses a template instantiates it, so each needs the whole body.

cards.q: When is a forward declaration of a class enough?
cards.a:
When the code only uses pointers or references to it

`class Engine;` is enough for `Engine*` or `Engine&`. Creating an `Engine` or calling its members needs the full definition.

cards.q: Why keep function bodies out of the header?
cards.a:
A changed body then recompiles one file, not every includer

It also hides the implementation. Short functions and templates are the exceptions that go in the header.
